title: Pipeline parts list
description: Every part of the pipeline, once, as data (pipeline-parts.json): what it does in the user's words, how it is checked and applied, what it needs first, its settings and secrets by name, its jobs, the steps only a person can do, and its documents. scripts/pipeline_parts.py checks the list against this schema and against the repository, and writes docs/PARTS.md from it.
$comment: A SHAPE, NOT A RULE BOOK. Cross-field rules live in scripts/pipeline_parts.py: a null command or document needs a reason, every path exists, every dependency is known and acyclic, every installer and job writer belongs to a part, a card exists in its installer, and a command names only a kit script with arguments from a fixed list. Secrets are NAMES only: a value has no field to go in.

schema.description: The marker. A reader that does not know it reads nothing.

parts.description: One entry per part, in install order.

path.description: A path relative to the kit's root.

command.description: A kit script and its arguments. The checker allows only scripts/ and a fixed list of arguments.

name.description: The part in the user's words, never an internal name.

internal_name.description: What the code and older pages call it.

does.description: One or two sentences on what it does for the user.

scope.description: Installed once per machine, or once per project.

state.description: Its state in the kit: live code, built and off by default, or designed only.

needs.description: Ids of the parts it needs first.

scripts.description: The kit scripts this part owns. Each script belongs to one part.

installer.description: The script a person runs to install it, or null.

apply.description: The command that applies it, or null.

no_command_reason.description: Why it has no installer, check or apply. Required when any is null.

restarts.description: What applying it may restart, in plain words.

file.description: The settings file it reads, by name.

example.description: The committed example of that file.

keys.description: The keys that matter most, each present in the example.

secrets.description: The keys and tokens it needs, by NAME. Never a value.

key.description: The settings key that holds the secret's name.

default_name.description: The name the example file gives it.

ends.description: When the key stops working: a year after it is made, on a date chosen when it is made, never, or the kit does not say.

clock.description: The name the health check uses for its end date in CREDENTIAL_EXPIRIES. Required unless ends is never.

date_from.description: One plain line: where a person reads the date. Required unless ends is never.

items.description: One job, as data, for the supervisor that will read the list: what runs, when, as whom, where it logs, and what switches it. A <KEY> in a value is that settings key's value; <dir of KEY> is its folder.

label.description: The job label as the code builds it.

from_key.description: The settings key the label comes from, or null when fixed.

command.description: The program and its arguments, as the installer writes them into the job today.

schedule.description: Every interval_key seconds, kept alive, or once at boot.

interval_key.description: The settings key that sets the interval; null unless schedule is interval.

switch.description: The settings key that switches the job, and the example file that holds it; null when none does.

switch_reason.description: Why no key switches it. Required when switch is null.

card_in.description: The installer whose card table holds the card.

kind.description: Only a person can do it, or it is a sign-off a machine could fake.

ceiling.description: Its first-pass ceiling. Null until one is chosen.

consent.description: The lines it adds to an install consent page.

missing.description: Why a document is missing, one reason per null.
